data.narrative:
Aigen is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kenny Lee and Richard Wurden, having raised approximately $23.7M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private frontier-tech peers in the robotics sector alongside one public reference point, providing triangulation across two methodologies.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $24M total-raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $45M. The peer-median approach references three same-sector, same-stage companies—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—establishing a median comparable valuation of $1.8B with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $38M (low), $898M (median), and $2.0B (high). The stage-progression result reflects Aigen's early capital base; the peer-median reflects valuations of maturer Series B robotics companies with established market traction. The 53x spread between low and high estimates reflects material uncertainty around Aigen's market position relative to better-capitalized peers. Key variables driving valuation include the company's proprietary technology differentiation, current revenue or customer concentration, and trajectory relative to the $1.6B–$2.0B peer band. Additional disclosure of operational metrics would narrow this range substantially.
